title: Your First Weekend at California State University-Northridge, Shared as Cards
description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence mixing practical campus orientation, recreation, public art, outdoor landmarks and nearby Valley history. Check seasonal schedules before setting out.

cards.title: Friday: Start at the USU
cards.subtitle: Learn the weekend hub before branching out
cards.notes: Walk the complex, identify its lounge spaces and locate the SRC entrance now; the USU stays open on both weekend days during fall and spring.
cards.short_summary: An opening orientation stop that puts recreation, study space and student services on your mental map.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN identifies the University Student Union as a student-centered complex containing facilities including the Games Room, Computer Lab, Oasis Wellness Center and Student Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: Fall/spring building hours are Friday 7 a.m.–7 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; summer/winter weekend hours are 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Check listed holiday closures.

cards.title: Friday: Play a Short Round
cards.subtitle: Use the weekday window for billiards or console play
cards.notes: Bring your CSUN identification and sign in at the desk; choose one game first because checked-out equipment carries a two-hour limit.
cards.short_summary: A time-boxed social stop with billiards, board games, consoles and gaming PCs in one named room.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Games Room page lists billiards, board and card games, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch and gaming PCs, with equipment offered first-come, first-served for up to two hours.
cards.access_notes: Fall and spring hours are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; the room is closed in summer. CSUN students may bring one guest, and patrons must sign in at the front desk.

cards.title: Friday: Cross the Orange Grove
cards.subtitle: Ease into campus through a five-acre landscape
cards.notes: Follow the decomposed-granite paths among the Valencia trees, keep fruit on the branches and use the walk to learn the campus’s northeast side.
cards.short_summary: A low-key outdoor transition through a surviving piece of the Valley’s agricultural landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN documents the Orange Grove as an approximately five-acre campus landscape with more than 400 Valencia orange trees and walkways that let visitors move among them.
cards.access_notes: The official page presents the grove as a place to visit, socialize and study but does not publish visitor hours; remain on established paths and observe campus postings.

cards.title: Saturday: Move at the SRC
cards.subtitle: Start the morning with an indoor track or court session
cards.notes: Confirm your membership access, pack workout clothes and choose one simple activity such as the indoor track instead of trying every facility at once.
cards.short_summary: A Saturday reset inside CSUN’s dedicated exercise and leisure facility.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN describes the Student Recreation Center as a 283,000-square-foot exercise and leisure facility; its FAQ lists courts, fitness equipment, an indoor track, climbing areas and pools.
cards.access_notes: Current fall, spring and summer weekend building hours are 9 a.m.–5 p.m. The SRC is controlled-access; members must scan in, and membership or special access is required.

cards.title: Saturday: See the Neighborhood Courts
cards.subtitle: Step beyond campus to a city recreation complex
cards.notes: Walk or arrange a ride to Lemarsh Street, scan the posted program schedule and use only facilities available for unscheduled public recreation.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood-facing counterpoint to campus recreation, with fields, courts and picnic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks lists Northridge Recreation Center at 18300 Lemarsh Street with sports fields, indoor and outdoor basketball courts, tennis courts and picnic tables.
cards.access_notes: The city lists Saturday hours of 8 a.m.–4 p.m. and Sunday as closed. Classes and reserved activities may require registration or fees; confirm open-use availability onsite.

cards.title: Saturday: Set Up Your Study Base
cards.subtitle: Learn where weekend academic work can happen
cards.notes: Enter on the main floor, locate technology help and study zones, then save the library hours page because semester and service-desk schedules differ.
cards.short_summary: A practical scouting stop for finding your future weekend study base before assignments begin.
cards.evidence_claim: The library states that its Learning Commons remains open whenever the University Library is open and provides technology-focused workshops and learning support.
cards.access_notes: Weekend hours vary by term and date. Consult the current calendar at https://library.csun.edu/hours before visiting; individual service desks may operate on shorter schedules.

cards.entity_name: The Museum of the San Fernando Valley
cards.title: Saturday: Add Valley Context
cards.subtitle: Connect Northridge to its wider regional history
cards.notes: Head west on Nordhoff Street, allow time for the ongoing exhibits and ask a docent which display offers the clearest introduction to Valley history.
cards.short_summary: A nearby museum stop that frames the university within the history, arts and culture of the San Fernando Valley.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s official site identifies its Northridge location, advertises ongoing history and culture exhibits, and states that admission and parking are free.
cards.source_title: Explore the San Fernando Valley Museum Today
cards.access_notes: The museum currently lists Saturday and Sunday hours of 11 a.m.–4 p.m. and Tuesday hours of 1–5 p.m. Verify the schedule before leaving campus.

cards.title: Saturday: Watch a Kinetic Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Pause outside The Soraya near sunset
cards.notes: Stand back from the reflecting pool and watch how the stainless-steel blades respond to air and changing light; keep walkways clear for other visitors.
cards.short_summary: A brief golden-hour encounter with George Rickey’s moving stainless-steel public artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN identifies George Rickey’s kinetic sculpture “Two Up, Two Down” in front of The Soraya and specifically recommends seeing it in early morning or at sunset.
cards.source_title: Treasures on Campus: Explore the Public Art Around CSUN’s Parklike Campus
cards.access_notes: The artwork is outdoors in front of The Soraya at campus-map coordinate E-1. The source calls the campus artworks enjoyable year-round but does not state formal access hours.

cards.title: Sunday: Find the Letterform Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Begin with John T. Banks’s campus-scale sign
cards.notes: Approach from inside campus near Zelzah and Nordhoff, view the letterforms from several angles and stay separated from traffic at the campus edge.
cards.short_summary: A Sunday photo-and-design stop centered on a large sculptural rendering of the university initials.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s public-art guide identifies John T. Banks’s “CSUN Sculpture” at the corner of Zelzah Avenue and Nordhoff Street, campus-map coordinate G-1.
cards.source_title: Treasures on Campus: Explore the Public Art Around CSUN’s Parklike Campus
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus artwork at coordinate G-1. The official guide describes the campus art as available to enjoy year-round but supplies no formal access hours.

cards.title: Sunday: Finish Beside the Pond
cards.subtitle: Close the loop where the grove and observatory meet
cards.notes: Use the bridge and established paths for one final campus pause; observe the pond and waterfall without feeding or disturbing resident wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A quiet final stop at the landscaped water feature embedded in the Orange Grove.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN documents the pond in the Orange Grove as an enlarged water feature with a waterfall, meandering stream bed and bridge, relocated there during 2007–08.
cards.access_notes: The pond is an outdoor campus feature within the Orange Grove. The official page does not publish hours, so visit in daylight and follow posted campus-access guidance.

warnings: Library hours change by academic term and date; check the live library calendar before following the Saturday sequence.
SRC entry is restricted to members or people with approved special access; enrolled-student access depends on current eligibility.
Outdoor campus sources do not publish formal visitor hours for the Orange Grove, public artworks or pond, so daylight visits are advised.
